cim: Keep the art out of artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: Keep the art out of artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Ever since the launch of public artificial intelligence apps, such as ChatGPT or Claude, the average human has been taking advantage of the technology to make funny images, write songs or make posters. People do this because they claim they don’t have the talent to do it themselves or they don’t want to pay a professional to do it.

When people use AI for these kinda of activities, it takes away the core value of art: expressing yourself and expressing your feelings as a human — something AI can never do.

AI also takes away countless jobs from several different creative fields all across the world. According to futurism.com, the U.S. has lost more than 200,000 jobs in creative industries since the use of AI became public.

Some careers that have been hit the hardest by the rise of AI are graphic designers, illustrators and videographers.

For graphic designers, they used to be the key figures for designing logos, websites, billboards and merchandise for companies, but that is no longer the case.

Every building I walk into on campus, I always see AI flyers on ad boards. Every other ad I see, whether on the TV or on my phone, is made by AI. Every time I go on Pinterest, I see ads selling AI merchandise.

Here at Baylor, there is a graphic design major and a graphic design club, and I’m sure plenty of those students would be willing to make a design or two for whatever a person or organization needs.

For illustrators, their jobs can be taken away simply by typing “Generate an image of a dog” or “Animate someone jump roping.”

There are studio art majors on campus, with most of those students having excellent drawing skills. I’m sure they would also be more than happy to make a drawing or a painting for whatever someone needs.

For videographers, they use their unique skills to make cool edits or to make advertisements for companies, which is something AI is yet to entirely capture.

Sure, there are a decent amount of AI commercials on TV, but they lack the interesting camera angles and transitions that only humans know how to utilize.

Something that all of these AI uses have in common is that they encourage the average person to not indulge themselves in their God-given talent to create.

Just because you aren’t good at art when you first start doesn’t mean that you will never be good at it. You have to keep going, you have to keep creating and keeping the human spark of creativity alive, whether you are good at it or not.

Don’t let the temptation of streamlining creative tasks with AI persuade you. Imagination is a muscle, and no art made with AI can replace human creation.

prioritas.cim_hu: Véleménycikk: Ne engedjük be a mesterséges intelligenciát a művészetbe
prioritas.lead_hu: Egy egyetemi lap szerzője szerint az AI-képek és dalok generálása elvéti a művészet lényegét, ami az emberi érzések és az önkifejezés bemutatása lenne.
